CHIEF COMPLAINT
Shortness of breath

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Rachel is a 48-year-old female presenting with shortness of breath that occurs with mild exercise or walking, such as walking up her driveway. She reports associated palpitations and dyspnea on exertion. She notes the symptoms are happening more frequently lately and is uncertain if they are related to her chronic back pain. She recently increased exercise to address weight gain from the COVID-19 pandemic. She denies other recent lifestyle changes or new allergies.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient denies other issues bothering her at this time.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
- Depression
- Chronic back pain
- Smoking history (2 packs per day previously, now reduced to approximately one cigarette per day)

MEDICATIONS
- Effexor (venlafaxine) for depression
- Gabapentin (Neurontin) for chronic back pain

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient is a smoker, currently smoking approximately one cigarette per day, down from two packs per day. She has been attempting lifestyle modifications with increased exercise and weight management.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Not documented
General: Alert and oriented
Lungs: Mild wheezes in all lung fields; otherwise normal exam

RESULTS
Pulmonary Function Tests: Consistent with possible asthma or COPD
Chest X-ray: Flattened diaphragm consistent with COPD findings

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD): Diagnosed based on pulmonary function tests, chest imaging, and clinical presentation. Patient started on Combivent (ipratropium/albuterol) two puffs twice daily as maintenance therapy. Albuterol inhaler prescribed two puffs as needed for acute shortness of breath. Prednisone taper pack prescribed.

Depression: Stable on current Effexor therapy. Continue current medication. Encouraged to pursue yoga for mood and back pain management.

Chronic Back Pain: Continue Gabapentin (Neurontin). Encouraged to increase physical activity including yoga.
